## Problem 1.2: Cooling an air stream

A stream of 200 kg/h of air is cooled from 150 °C to 40 °C at constant
pressure with no phase change. Taking the specific heat capacity of air as
$c_p = 1.005\ \text{kJ}\,\text{kg}^{-1}\,\text{K}^{-1}$, determine the
cooling duty in kW.

::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions"}
**Solution**

Sensible heat only:

$$\dot{Q} = \dot{m}\,c_p\,\Delta T
= (200)(1.005)(40 - 150) = -22{,}110\ \text{kJ/h}.$$

The negative sign indicates heat removed. As a cooling duty:

$$|\dot{Q}| = \frac{22{,}110\ \text{kJ/h}}{3600\ \text{s/h}} \approx 6.14\ \text{kW}.$$
:::
